tasks.short: Turn market and search evidence into product requirements with design and engineering.

steps.what: Review search, conversion and customer trends in the {BI}.
Read market research and customer feedback in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved market research, customer feedback and performance snapshot.
loop.output: Evidence notes linking needs, contradictory findings and gaps to source passages.
loop.check: Validate source references; strategist checks consequential findings and unsupported interpretations.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass per document; unreadable sources return to the strategist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text research expresses needs and qualifications that fixed fields do not capture.

steps.what: Agree user problems, feasibility constraints and priorities with design and engineering.
Write requirements and acceptance criteria in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Agreed priorities, cited evidence, constraints and a requirements template.
loop.output: Requirements draft with measurable acceptance criteria and explicit unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check required sections and evidence links; strategist verifies intent and testability.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision against review comments; unresolved trade-offs remain marked.
loop.why_not_simpler: Translating varied user needs into clear requirements requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Approve requirements and resolve scope trade-offs.
Transfer approved requirements and evidence links into the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configure a reusable evidence view in the {BI}; bounded loops turn approved material in the {DOCS} into cited evidence notes and a requirements draft. People settle priorities and approve scope, after which a deterministic integration creates linked records in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered, research language varied, and copying approved requirements between systems needed custom glue.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and document interfaces support a small reusable workflow. AI-assisted coding can reduce connector and validation work; bounded extraction and drafting reduce document preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Search demand does not prove a product need. Sparse research, conflicting stakeholder goals and engineering uncertainty still require investigation and negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Connect market evidence to a worthwhile user problem and negotiate a feasible scope without disguising uncertainty.

ambition.what: A pre-build search-demand assessment for proposed product features.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends more time testing product hypotheses with design and engineering. They can recommend evidence-backed acceptance criteria; product scope and funding remain with the product manager.

reach.task: Translate a user problem into a testable interaction requirement.
reach.learn: User flows, accessibility requirements and prototype evaluation.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Plan research that distinguishes expressed interest from an unmet need.
reach.learn: Sampling, interview design and limits of inference.

evidence.claim: Configured dashboards and deterministic record creation can handle structured evidence preparation and backlog transfer.
Bounded extraction and drafting can prepare requirements; source validation and human scope decisions remain necessary.

assumptions: This is occasional product discovery work within a larger marketing role.
A product manager has final scope authority.
The initial build uses aggregate data and approved research, with manual file import where connectors are unavailable.
Build ranges cover one reusable workflow and a small pilot, not a research repository migration.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply; national rules govern any employee consultation required by the actual deployment.
unknowns: Which research and performance sources are available and reliable?
Can existing access permissions be preserved during extraction?
Who can approve requirements and create delivery records?
Does the proposed data use require employee consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can reviewers trace every consequential requirement to evidence or an explicitly labelled hypothesis?
Does the existing {PROJECT} already support approved document-to-backlog transfer?
new_work: Review extracted findings and draft acceptance criteria.
Resolve missing evidence and conflicting research.
Maintain document templates, source permissions and backlog field mappings.
Check whether implemented features answer the original user problem.

tasks.short: Set up, launch and improve display or video advertising campaigns.

steps.what: Define campaign objectives, audience, budget and measurement in the {DOCS}.
Collect approved creative files and destination links from the {DOCS}.
Enter targeting, placements, tracking and creative into draft campaigns in the {ADS}.
Review campaign previews, targeting, budget and measurement before authorizing launch.
Activate the approved campaign in the {ADS}.
Combine delivery, spend and conversion exports in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Choose creative tests, exclusions and budget changes from campaign results.
Apply approved campaign changes in the {ADS}.

tasks.design: Use templates and native rules in the {ADS} to create paused campaigns from approved assets in the {DOCS}, with deterministic checks for budgets, dates, links and tracking. A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles exports into the {BI}; launch and campaign edits require approval of the exact settings, and changed settings invalidate that approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Campaign setup was repetitive, while reporting crossed incompatible exports and conversion definitions. Creative and budget decisions also obscured the parts that could already be configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Native campaign templates handle much of setup. Small coded connectors and validation rules can now be cheaper to build and maintain; no model loop is needed for the proposed scope.
tasks.still_hard: Attribution, delayed conversions, creative fatigue and misleading short-term results still make optimization uncertain. Approval and tracking requirements vary by audience and market.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the commercial objective, judge creative fit and distinguish a useful test result from noise.

ambition.what: A weekly creative-test allocation decision using reconciled delivery and conversion data.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less time entering settings and assembling reports, and more time designing experiments with creative colleagues. They gain a regular test-allocation recommendation; spending authority stays within the existing delegation.

reach.task: Write a creative test brief with a clear visual hypothesis.
reach.learn: Visual hierarchy, asset specifications and controlled creative variation.

reach.task: Evaluate campaign investment against incremental business outcomes.
reach.learn: Experiment design, contribution margin and uncertainty in attribution.

evidence.claim: Campaign templates, budget rules and draft states can automate repetitive setup where the {ADS} exposes them.
Deterministic reconciliation can replace spreadsheet report assembly without automating campaign strategy.

assumptions: Creative production is handled separately; this task starts with approved assets.
The initial scope covers one advertising account and existing conversion measurement.
Native templates and rules are tried before custom campaign-writing integrations.
Launch approval in s4 is the approval consumed by s5, not a second approval round.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply. Tracking consent and national rules must be reflected in the permitted data and targeting.
Run cost excludes advertising spend and existing software subscriptions.
unknowns: Which draft, approval and change-control capabilities exist in the {ADS}?
Who holds launch and budget-change authority?
Are conversion definitions consistent across the {ADS} and {BI}?
Which audience uses, tracking consents and data transfers are currently permitted?
Does connecting data introduce employee monitoring requiring consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can native templates cover the actual campaign types without custom write access?
Can an approval be bound to immutable campaign settings?
What reporting delay is needed before a test decision is meaningful?
new_work: Review exact launch and change previews.
Handle rejected assets, failed imports and tracking discrepancies.
Maintain naming conventions, templates and metric mappings.
Check spend limits and reconcile discrepancies after deployment.

tasks.short: Evaluate marketing suppliers and support negotiation of vendor or partner contracts.

steps.what: Gather supplier proposals, contract versions and service history from the {EMAIL}.
Compare fees, commitments and service metrics in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Review scope, termination, measurement and data clauses in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Versioned contract draft, approved playbook and commercial comparison.
loop.output: Cited clause table, missing provisions and possible deviations requiring review.
loop.check: Verify quotations and locations; strategist checks service terms and refers legal issues to legal counsel.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; ambiguous or missing clauses remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Equivalent obligations appear in varied language and cross-referenced clauses.

steps.what: Agree negotiating priorities and concession limits.
Discuss service commitments and concessions with the supplier.
Document the recommendation, concessions and unresolved issues in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Verified negotiation notes, clause issues and calculated commercial comparison.
loop.output: Recommendation draft separating agreed points, proposed concessions and unresolved issues.
loop.check: Match amounts to calculations and commitments to notes; strategist verifies the recommendation.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported commitments are omitted and flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Negotiation notes need contextual synthesis into a concise recommendation.

steps.what: Approve the commercial recommendation or request further negotiation.

tasks.design: Configure an intake folder in the {DOCS} from selected {EMAIL} threads, then calculate commercial comparisons from verified structured fields. Bounded loops prepare cited clause issues and recommendations; people set the mandate, negotiate and approve the commercial decision, with approved records stored in the {CLM} where available.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier terms arrived as inconsistent documents, versions were hard to track, and bespoke comparison tools were expensive for occasional use.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can produce reviewable clause tables, while inexpensive deterministic tools handle calculations and version checks. A small reusable pack can start from files without replacing procurement systems.
tasks.still_hard: Legal interpretation, bargaining power, hidden dependencies and supplier credibility remain difficult. Scanned documents, complex fee schedules and conflicting versions can erase preparation savings.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the supplier relationship, trade concessions deliberately and recognize commitments that need legal or commercial escalation.

ambition.what: A marketing-supplier measurement-terms review before commercial approval.

tasks.altitude: The strategist brings a clearer view of measurement rights, service commitments and total cost to negotiations. They gain influence over service acceptance criteria; contract signature and legal approval remain with authorized roles.

reach.task: Assess the commercial value and measurement obligations of a marketing supplier.
reach.learn: Total-cost scenarios, service acceptance criteria and negotiation preparation.

evidence.claim: Structured fee comparisons and version checks are deterministic; clause extraction needs review against source text.
The digest documents automated procurement negotiation, but does not establish suitability for bespoke marketing contracts.

assumptions: The strategist supports procurement rather than holding contract-signing authority.
Legal review is a separate dependency and is not replaced by clause extraction.
Negotiation conversations stay within the approved mandate; binding commitments follow the existing signature process.
Commercial calculations use verified structured fields; extracted amounts require confirmation before calculation.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply. Confidential documents use approved processing arrangements and existing access restrictions.
The access range includes consultation under national rules if the actual deployment requires it.
unknowns: Which contract playbook and concession limits are approved?
Is a {CLM} available, or are contracts held in the {DOCS}?
Who provides legal review and commercial approval?
Can confidential supplier documents be processed in the proposed environment?
Are contract versions and commercial assumptions reliably identified?
research_questions: Which clause types can be extracted reliably from representative supplier contracts?
Can existing {CLM} configuration cover intake, comparisons and approval records?
What minimum review is needed to prevent an omitted clause from appearing acceptable?
new_work: Verify extracted clauses, fee fields and document versions.
Maintain the approved playbook and commercial comparison rules.
Escalate ambiguous terms and unsupported commitments.
Record final negotiated changes against the reviewed version.

tasks.short: Create e-commerce storyboards and prototypes to test search-led customer journeys.

steps.what: Clarify the audience, journey and test objective in the {DOCS}.
Collect approved product information, images and brand components from the {DOCS}.
Write the storyboard and page messages in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Prototype brief, approved product facts, assets and allowed component catalogue.
loop.output: Storyboard, source-linked page messages and a structured component layout.
loop.check: Validate layout schema, asset references and allowed components; strategist checks narrative and claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or unavailable components remain flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning a journey objective into a coherent storyboard and short copy requires contextual writing.

steps.what: Assemble screens and interactions in a graphics editor in the {OTHER}.
Refine composition, responsive layouts and interactions in a graphics editor in the {OTHER}.
Review the prototype with design and engineering and select a test direction.
Export annotated screens and handoff files from a graphics editor in the {OTHER}.

tasks.design: A bounded loop drafts a storyboard and validated component layout from approved material in the {DOCS}. A deterministic renderer assembles an editable prototype in the graphics-editor category of {OTHER}; people refine the design and select the test direction, then configured exports produce the handoff pack.
tasks.previous_blocker: Even simple prototypes required repeated layout assembly, asset preparation and export work. Bespoke visual choices made the entire task appear unsuitable for automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable components and structured layout formats make assembly predictable. AI-assisted coding can lower the cost of a small renderer, while a bounded loop prepares the narrative and copy.
tasks.still_hard: Distinctive visual work, complex interactions and realistic responsive behaviour still take skilled effort. A template prototype may hide usability problems or look more complete than it is.
tasks.human_edge: Judge visual hierarchy, choose a convincing journey and notice when a prototype communicates the wrong promise.

ambition.what: A search-intent landing-page prototype clinic before campaign launch.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends more time testing page messages and journeys with designers, with less screen assembly and export work. They can propose prototype experiments; production design and release authority stay with the relevant owners.

reach.task: Build and evaluate a responsive interaction prototype.
reach.learn: Component systems, accessibility, responsive behaviour and usability testing.

reach.task: Evaluate product-page information and purchase-path friction.
reach.learn: Product information quality, merchandising priorities and checkout constraints.

evidence.claim: Component-based rendering and configured exports can automate assembly of constrained prototypes.
Bounded drafting can prepare a storyboard and copy, while visual refinement and test selection remain human work.

assumptions: The first version covers one landing-page family using an existing component and brand library.
The graphics editor supports editable imports or a suitable extension interface.
The storyboard review confirms the structured layout before rendering.
Prototypes use approved assets and synthetic customer examples; publishing a live page is outside this task.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply. Employee consultation under national rules is included if required by the actual rollout.
Missing components or extensive custom animation would increase the build range.
unknowns: Which graphics editor, import formats and extension permissions are available?
Is there an approved component library and asset-rights register?
Who approves a prototype for user testing?
How often do prototypes require layouts outside the proposed component catalogue?
research_questions: Can existing editor configuration cover assembly before a custom renderer is built?
Does the generated prototype preserve useful editability and responsive behaviour?
Can reviewers distinguish placeholder interactions from behaviour ready for testing?
new_work: Review storyboard claims and component choices.
Refine visual hierarchy and test interaction behaviour.
Maintain component mappings, asset references and export settings.
Label placeholders and record what each prototype actually tests.

role.altitude: The week shifts toward experiment design, market interpretation, supplier trade-offs and collaboration with design and engineering. The strategist can propose product acceptance criteria and campaign tests more confidently; budget, contract, product-scope and release authority remain with their existing owners unless explicitly delegated.
reach: Web and Digital Interface Designers: turn search intent into testable journeys and prototypes.
Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists: design research that tests product hypotheses.
Advertising and Promotions Managers: assess campaign tests and investment choices.
Online Merchants: connect product information and purchase friction to search demand.
skills_to_grow: Metric definitions, attribution limits and data-quality diagnosis.
Requirements writing and testable acceptance criteria.
Responsive design, accessibility and prototype evaluation.
Reviewing bounded model outputs and maintaining deterministic rules.
role.ambitious_version: Run a search-to-journey experimentation service that connects observed demand, product hypotheses, landing-page prototypes and campaign tests, with explicit approvals for spending, commitments and production changes.
